passages.text: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah had reigned for fourteen years.
Sennacherib was king of Assyria.
Sennacherib attacked Judah.
Judah had many fortified cities.
Sennacherib captured all the fortified cities of Judah.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י בְּאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ עָלָ֞ה סַנְחֵרִ֤יב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁוּר֙ עַ֣ל כָּל־ עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה הַבְּצֻר֖וֹת וַֽיִּתְפְּשֵֽׂם׃

passages.text: And the king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh, with a great army, from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. And he stopped by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem.
He sent him to King Hezekiah.
The Rabshakeh brought a great army with him.
He stopped at the aqueduct of the upper pool.
This place was on the road to the Launderer’s Field.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֣וּר׀ אֶת־ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֨ה מִלָּכִ֧ישׁ יְרוּשָׁלְַ֛מָה אֶל־ הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּחֵ֣יל כָּבֵ֑ד וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֗ד בִּתְעָלַת֙ הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הָעֶלְיוֹנָ֔ה בִּמְסִלַּ֖ת שְׂדֵ֥ה כוֹבֵֽס׃

passages.text: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to him.
passages.sermon:
Eliakim was the son of Hilkiah.
Eliakim was the palace administrator.
Shebna was the scribe.
Joah was the son of Asaph.
Joah was the recorder.
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah went out to meet the Rabshakeh.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֵלָ֛יו אֶלְיָקִ֥ים בֶּן־ חִלְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ הַבָּ֑יִת וְשֶׁבְנָא֙ הַסֹּפֵ֔ר וְיוֹאָ֥ח בֶּן־ אָסָ֖ף הַמַּזְכִּֽיר׃

passages.text: The Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah that this is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is the basis of this confidence of yours?
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh spoke to the men.
He was the chief officer sent by the king of Assyria.
He said, “Go and tell Hezekiah this message.
The king of Assyria is a powerful king.
He calls himself the great king.
He asks Hezekiah a question.
He says, ‘What is the reason for your confidence?
Why do you trust so strongly?’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֔ה אִמְרוּ־ נָ֖א אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר מָ֧ה הַבִּטָּח֛וֹן הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּטָֽחְתָּ׃

passages.text: You claim to have a strategy and strength for war, but these are empty words. In whom are you now trusting, that you have rebelled against me?
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh spoke to the messengers from Hezekiah.
He was the chief officer of the king of Assyria.
He said, “You say you have advice and strength for war.
But these are only words.
You do not have real power.
You do not have real plans.
Now, tell me, who are you trusting?
Why have you rebelled against me?”
passages.original: אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ אַךְ־ דְּבַר־ שְׂפָתַ֔יִם עֵצָ֥ה וּגְבוּרָ֖ה לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ עַל־ מִ֣י בָטַ֔חְתָּ כִּ֥י מָרַ֖דְתָּ בִּֽי׃

passages.text: Look now, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
passages.sermon:
You are trusting in Egypt.
Egypt is like a broken reed.
A broken reed cannot support anyone.
If a person leans on this reed, it will pierce his hand.
Pharaoh is the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh harms all who trust in him.
Everyone who relies on Pharaoh will be hurt.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה בָטַ֡חְתָּ עַל־ מִשְׁעֶנֶת֩ הַקָּנֶ֨ה הָרָצ֤וּץ הַזֶּה֙ עַל־ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִסָּמֵ֥ךְ אִישׁ֙ עָלָ֔יו וּבָ֥א בְכַפּ֖וֹ וּנְקָבָ֑הּ כֵּ֚ן פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֔יִם לְכָֽל־ הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: But if you say to me, ‘We trust in the LORD our God,’ is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship before this altar’?
passages.sermon:
You may say to me, "We trust in the LORD our God."
Hezekiah is the king of Judah.
Hezekiah removed the high places and altars of the LORD.
Hezekiah told Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship before this altar."
Is this not the same God in whom you now trust?
passages.original: וְכִי־ תֹאמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י אֶל־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ בָּטָ֑חְנוּ הֲלוֹא־ ה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵסִ֤יר חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶת־ בָּמֹתָ֣יו וְאֶת־ מִזְבְּחֹתָ֔יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לִֽיהוּדָה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִפְנֵ֛י הַמִּזְבֵּ֥חַ הַזֶּ֖ה תִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֽוּ׃

passages.text: Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria is powerful.
He sends his official to speak.
The official challenges Judah.
He says, “Make an agreement with my master, the king of Assyria.
I will give you two thousand horses.
You must find riders to put on them.
If you cannot find riders, you cannot use the horses.
This shows your weakness.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ הִתְעָ֣רֶב נָ֔א אֶת־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לְךָ֙ אַלְפַּ֣יִם סוּסִ֔ים אִם־ תּוּכַ֕ל לָ֥תֶת לְךָ֖ רֹכְבִ֥ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For how can you repel a single officer among the least of my master’s servants when you depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh is a high official from the king of Assyria.
He speaks to the leaders of Judah.
He says, “You trust in Egypt for help.
You hope Egypt will give you chariots and horsemen.
But you cannot defeat even one of my master’s lowest officers.
You cannot stand against even the least of the king of Assyria’s servants.
You depend on Egypt, but that will not save you.”
passages.original: וְאֵ֣יךְ תָּשִׁ֗יב אֵ֠ת פְּנֵ֨י פַחַ֥ת אַחַ֛ד עַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י הַקְטַנִּ֑ים וַתִּבְטַ֤ח לְךָ֙ עַל־ מִצְרַ֔יִם לְרֶ֖כֶב וּלְפָרָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: So now, was it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this land to destroy it? The LORD Himself said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh was the chief officer of the king of Assyria.
He spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
He said, “I did not come to attack this land without the LORD’s command.
The LORD told me to come up against this land.
The LORD said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ הֲמִבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עָלִ֛יתִי עַל־ הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את לְהַשְׁחִיתָ֑הּ יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י עֲלֵ֛ה אֶל־ הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את וְהַשְׁחִיתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall.”
passages.sermon:
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah served King Hezekiah of Judah.
They spoke to the Rabshakeh, who was the chief officer of the king of Assyria.
They said, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic.
We understand the Aramaic language.
Do not speak to us in Hebrew.
The people on the wall can hear Hebrew.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִים֩ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל־ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֗ה דַּבֶּר־ נָ֤א אֶל־ עֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲרָמִ֔ית כִּ֥י שֹׁמְעִ֖ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וְאַל־ תְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלֵ֙ינוּ֙ יְהוּדִ֔ית בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ הַחוֹמָֽה׃

passages.text: But the Rabshakeh replied, “Has my master sent me to speak these words only to you and your master, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are destined with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh was a high official from the king of Assyria.
He spoke to Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah.
He answered their request.
He said, “My master did not send me only to your lord and to you.
He sent me also to the men sitting on the wall.
These men will suffer with you.
They will eat their own dung.
They will drink their own urine with you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר רַב־ שָׁקֵ֗ה הַאֶ֨ל אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ וְאֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲדֹנִ֔י לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲלֹ֣א עַל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ עַל־ הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת־ חַרְאֵיהֶם וְלִשְׁתּ֛וֹת אֶת־ שֵׁינֵיהֶם עִמָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Hebrew: “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh was a high official from Assyria.
He stood before the people of Jerusalem.
He spoke in a loud voice.
He spoke in Hebrew.
He said, “Listen to the words of the great king.
The great king is the king of Assyria.”
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְקוֹל־ גָּד֖וֹל יְהוּדִ֑ית וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְע֗וּ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הַגָּד֖וֹל מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot deliver you.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
He said, “Do not let Hezekiah deceive you.
Hezekiah cannot save you.
He cannot deliver you from my power.”
passages.original: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אַל־ יַשִּׁ֥א לָכֶ֖ם חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּ֥י לֹֽא־ יוּכַ֖ל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD when he says, ‘The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria sent his official, the Rabshakeh, to speak to the people of Jerusalem.
He spoke loudly in Hebrew.
He said, “Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD.
Hezekiah may say, ‘The LORD will surely deliver us.’
He may say, ‘This city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’
Do not believe him.”
passages.original: וְאַל־ יַבְטַ֨ח אֶתְכֶ֤ם חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר הַצֵּ֥ל יַצִּילֵ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then every one of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink water from his own cistern, until I come and take you away to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He says, “Do not listen to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah is your king.
Hezekiah tells you to trust the LORD.
But I, the king of Assyria, say this.
Make peace with me.
Come out to me.
If you do this, each of you will eat from your own vine.
Each of you will eat from your own fig tree.
Each of you will drink water from your own cistern.
You will have these things until I come.
Then I will take you away to another land.
This land will be like your own land.
It will be a land of grain and new wine.
It will be a land of bread and vineyards.”
passages.original: אַֽל־ תִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּס כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר עֲשֽׂוּ־ אִתִּ֤י בְרָכָה֙ וּצְא֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְאִכְל֤וּ אִישׁ־ גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּאֵנָת֔וֹ וּשְׁת֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ מֵי־ בוֹרֽוֹ׃ עַד־ בֹּאִ֕י וְלָקַחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּאַרְצְכֶ֑ם אֶ֤רֶץ דָּגָן֙ וְתִיר֔וֹשׁ אֶ֥רֶץ לֶ֖חֶם וּכְרָמִֽים׃

passages.text: Do not let Hezekiah mislead you when he says, ‘The LORD will deliver us.’ Has the god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
He warned them about Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah trusted in the LORD.
The king of Assyria said, “Do not let Hezekiah mislead you.”
Hezekiah says, ‘The LORD will deliver us.’
The king of Assyria asked a question.
He said, “Has the god of any nation ever saved his land from the king of Assyria?”
No other nation’s god has delivered them from Assyria.
The king of Assyria claimed the LORD would not save Jerusalem.
passages.original: פֶּן־ יַסִּ֨ית אֶתְכֶ֤ם חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֖ה יַצִּילֵ֑נוּ הַהִצִּ֜ילוּ אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ אַרְצ֔וֹ מִיַּ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria spoke.
He challenged the people of Jerusalem.
He asked about the gods of Hamath.
He asked about the gods of Arpad.
He asked about the gods of Sepharvaim.
He questioned their power.
He asked, “Where are these gods?”
He asked if these gods saved Samaria from his hand.
He implied that these gods did not save their people.
He suggested that no god had stopped him.
passages.original: אַיֵּ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י חֲמָת֙ וְאַרְפָּ֔ד אַיֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י סְפַרְוָ֑יִם וְכִֽי־ הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־ שֹׁמְר֖וֹן מִיָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand? How then can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?”
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria spoke.
He asked about the gods of many nations.
He said, “No god has saved any land from my power.
No god has delivered his people from my hand.
He questioned the LORD’s power.
He said, “How can the LORD save Jerusalem from me?”
passages.original: מִ֗י בְּכָל־ אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָֽאֲרָצוֹת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־ הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־ אַרְצָ֖ם מִיָּדִ֑י כִּֽי־ יַצִּ֧יל יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: But the people remained silent and did not answer a word, for Hezekiah had commanded, “Do not answer him.”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah gave a command to the people.
Hezekiah said, “Do not answer him.”
The people heard Hezekiah’s command.
The people remained silent.
The people did not answer him at all.
passages.original: וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ וְלֹֽא־ עָנ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ דָּבָ֑ר כִּֽי־ מִצְוַ֨ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הִ֛יא לֵאמֹ֖ר לֹ֥א תַעֲנֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Then Hilkiah’s son Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Asaph’s son Joah the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they relayed to him the words of the Rabshakeh.
passages.sermon:
Eliakim was the son of Hilkiah.  
Eliakim served as the palace administrator.  
Shebna was the scribe.  
Joah was the son of Asaph.  
Joah served as the recorder.  
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah went to King Hezekiah.  
Their clothes were torn.  
They told Hezekiah the words of the Rabshakeh.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן־ חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ אֲשֶׁר־ עַל־ הַ֠בַּיִת וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א הַסּוֹפֵ֜ר וְיוֹאָ֨ח בֶּן־ אָסָ֧ף הַמַּזְכִּ֛יר אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י רַב־ שָׁקֵֽה׃ס
